key_insight: GTAFL addresses long-tailed federated learning when both training data are class-imbalanced and test-time class distributions are unknown.
clinical_relevance: The framework could make decentralized medical-image models more robust to changing disease-class frequencies across healthcare settings, though clinical benefit is not established.
method: Adaptive re-sampling and expert classifier retraining address class-imbalance bias.
Self-supervised learning targets distorted feature representations.
An inference-time ensemble combines retrained experts for unknown test distributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports outperforming state-of-the-art methods on CIFAR10 and two medical datasets, without naming the medical datasets or providing numerical results.
watch_item: Robustness to unknown class distributions in benchmarks does not establish performance under broader real-world clinical shifts.
paper_title: GTAFL: Addressing Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning in Medical Image
